items.title: Louis Keppard Interview, 1961-01-19
items.q: I'd say, good morning, Mr. Willey. Good morning.

ctx.x: It's hard on your voice, I guess, to try to talk up too high, isn't it?

Yeah, I used to take it, sometime I'd get around, I used to see a woman come to see her, and I'd get out there and I'd see them coming in the front door or something, and they'd go in around. I'd say, good morning, Mr. Willey. Good morning. Oh, that's the old one. And then I'd put my hands over my mother. Listen, Willey, do you find it across, eh? Yes, ma'am. I said, well, all right, bring me a pong of red beans. Oh, that's the... Maybe you're right, huh? Yeah. You want to go back there and talk with her, you…

I was gonna ask you for one thing, if we have room here, if not we'll do it on another reel, if you have a few minutes yet. If you could tell us anything about the dancing in the old... Well, the dancing... ...the old times. I mean, what kind of steps did they use, or is it much different than now?
